title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

reports.title: Error by AI scribe during medical appointment leaves patient devastated

summary:
Rebecca Green agreed to let an AI scribe transcribe her first urologist appointment in Australia, but the tool invented a false claim that she used psychedelic mushrooms. She discovered the error only after kidney stone surgery, when a post-operative letter to her GP said micro-dosing could explain earlier kidney bleeding. She feared this could hurt her workers’ compensation case. The urologist later apologised, corrected the record, and said she would review how AI was used, but did not answer questions about any changes.

Privacy advocates say such AI hallucinations are a growing risk, with one report citing a wrong breast recorded in a cancer case and a false epilepsy diagnosis. The Royal Australian College of GPs estimates about 40 percent of GPs regularly use AI scribes. Australia’s medicines regulator is reviewing these tools and will release findings in coming weeks, with breaches to be acted on. Advocacy groups want approved AI scribe lists and stronger consent rules. Ms Green says she would only consent again with a doctor she already knows.
